question: For $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$, verify that $-2(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=(-2\vec{a})+(-2\vec{b})$.
explanation:
Step 1: Evaluation inside the brackets
\(\vec{a}+\vec{b}=\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}\)
Therefore,
\(-2(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=-2\hat{i}-6\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\)
Step 2: Individual scalar multiplication
\(-2\vec{a}=-4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-6\hat{k}\)
and
\(-2\vec{b}=2\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
Step 3: Addition of the scalar multiples
\((-2\vec{a})+(-2\vec{b})=-2\hat{i}-6\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\)
Step 4: Comparison
Both sides give the same vector.
Final Answer
$-2(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=(-2\vec{a})+(-2\vec{b})=-2\hat{i}-6\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$.

options.C: The left side is $-2\hat{i}-6\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ while the right side is $2\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$.
